rules.source_guideline: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Congestive Heart Failure
rules.guideline_quote: In cardiogenic pulmonary edema, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure leads to pulmonary vascular redistribution, interstitial/alveolar edema, and frequently secondary pleural effusions.

rules.source_guideline: Fleischner Society: Glossary of Terms for Thoracic Imaging
rules.guideline_quote: Airspace consolidation represents dense opacification of the pulmonary parenchyma and is almost universally accompanied by contiguous airspace infiltration.

rules.source_guideline: ATS/ERS International Multidisciplinary Consensus on Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
rules.guideline_quote: End-stage pulmonary fibrosis induces parenchymal volume loss, traction bronchiectasis, and reactive apical/subpleural pleural thickening.

rules.source_guideline: ATS/IDSA Guidelines on the Management of Community-Acquired Pneumonia
rules.guideline_quote: The radiographic hallmark of bacterial pneumonia is lobar or segmental consolidation co-occurring with inflammatory infiltration.

rules.source_guideline: ACC/AHA Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
rules.guideline_quote: Decompensated biventricular failure with pronounced cardiomegaly and pleural effusion carries a high likelihood of concurrent alveolar pulmonary edema.

rules.source_guideline: British Thoracic Society (BTS) Pleural Disease Guidelines
rules.guideline_quote: In secondary spontaneous pneumothorax complicating chronic obstructive pulmonary disease/emphysema, air entry into the pleural space results in compressive atelectasis of the underlying lung.
